title: Celebrate Cinema 2026 Brings 4,000 Students Face to Face with Film Industry Leaders at Whistling Woods
summary: The three-day festival at Whistling Woods International featured Aamir Khan, Hema Malini, Imtiaz Ali and Rana Daggubati, and a scholarship announced in Dharmendra's name.
body_html:
Mumbai, 14 October 2026: Whistling Woods International (WWI) hosted the 14th edition of Celebrate Cinema from 7 to 9 October on the theme "Impact of Big-Screen Cinema". The open festival brought together more than 4,000 students, industry professionals and creative minds.

The festival opened with Aamir Khan, Aparna Purohit and the Sitaare Zameen Par team discussing storytelling and the theatrical experience. Over three days, more than 15 industry experts took part in discussions, alongside more than eight masterclasses and over 50 workshops on subjects from screenwriting and editing to VFX, sound, animation and AI tools for filmmaking.

Speakers included Hema Malini, Imtiaz Ali, Rana Daggubati, Jyoti Deshpande, Siddharth Roy Kapur, Sriram Raghavan and experts from Sony Pictures, Warner Bros. Discovery, Google and Adobe. An Immersive Studio showed VR, motion capture and projection mapping installations.

Hema Malini inaugurated an exhibition honouring veteran actor Dharmendra, with a tribute that included an audiovisual presentation made by WWI students. Maharashtra's Minister of Cultural Affairs, Ashish Shelar, announced mid-term scholarships in Dharmendra's name for academically excelling WWI students, and paid tribute to actor Nana Patekar.

"Through Celebrate Cinema, I want our young filmmakers to learn this craft, find their own voice and create stories that audiences will want to experience on the big screen," said Subhash Ghai, Founder and Chairman, WWI.

"Celebrate Cinema is where education meets inspiration," said Meghna Ghai Puri, President, WWI. The festival closed with filmmaker Imtiaz Ali in conversation with Subhash Ghai.
